title: Immersive Schema Editor Onboarding — micro-interactions, inline recovery, and visual diffs
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Create a set of onboarding and quickstart UX assets for the immersive Schema Editor focused on micro-interactions, inline validation recovery, and a visual diffing experience for schema evolution. Deliverables: a short interactive prototype (Figma + simple animated GIFs), a set of annotated screenshots for docs, accessibility notes, and handoff tokens for engineering. Goal is to reduce time-to-first-success for users authoring structured-output JSON Schemas while surfacing low-friction recovery when validation fails.
acceptance_criteria: Figma prototype includes first-run tour with 5 annotated micro-interactions: inline hint chips, live example preview, auto-suggest types, quick-fix actions, schema-change diff rail.
Three exported 1200x800 screenshots (desktop) and one 640x360 mobile screenshot annotated for docs and release notes.
Animated GIFs (max 8s each) demonstrating: (1) inline validation + quick-fix, (2) visual diff when updating schema version, (3) keyboard-first navigation for power users.
Accessibility audit notes covering color contrast, focus order, and ARIA labels for interactive chips.
Handoff checklist with CSS variables, Lottie or sprite guidance for micro-animations, and a GitHub PR template for engineering work.
Design review approved by PM (Riley Gupta) and ENG owner (Sofia Alvarez).
tasks: Design first-run tour (3 slides) highlighting: live preview, quick-fix, diff rail
Create micro-animation specs for inline chips (duration, easing, reduced-motion alternative)
Build annotated screenshots for docs (desktop + mobile)
Prepare Figma prototype and export GIFs for the release notes
Write accessibility notes and add to the component spec
Collaborate with ENG on keyboard shortcuts and telemetry hooks
decisions: Inline quick-fix action will apply a non-destructive suggestion that users can accept or undo (opted for undo rather than auto-commit).
Diff rail will appear on schema version changes only and show inline color-coded additions/deletions rather than a full-side-by-side diff to reduce cognitive load.
Micro-animations will default to 160ms ease-out; reduced-motion users get instant state changes (no animation).
Validation chips will include explicit error severity badges (info/warning/error) to help triage at glance.
